notes:
Summary: Mid-market product analytics company evaluating Redwood for primary inference layer. Started on Hosted API to validate models (embeddings + reranking + support chat). POC successful for quality; biggest question is economics at scale and predictable latency.

Usage profile and technical asks:
- POC: ~600M tokens/month equivalent; expect growth to ~1.2B tokens/mo within 9 months if conversion to dedicated.
- Latency SLO: target p50 <= 150ms for short-turn chat & reranking flows; p95 target <= 350ms. Current hosted POC p50=160ms, p95=320ms.
- Throughput target: baseline 80-120 requests/sec across multi-tenant product features (peak spikes during release windows).
- Models: prefer Llama-3 70B quantized for primary quality, accept 13B / 7B variants for burst/fallback. Need support for KV cache and quantized kernels.
- Routing/fallback: automatic fallback to smaller model family when committed capacity saturated; require fallback behavior defined in SLA.

Pricing & packaging negotiation notes (procurement focus):
- Committed configuration asked for: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (baseline) + burst pool up to 2x for short spikes. Proposed ramp: month1=50% commit, month2=75%, month3=100% (to reduce initial cash out).
- Redwood proposed pricing anchors in dedicated_proposal_v2.pdf: commit discount tiers at 6, 12, 24 months; 6-month minimal term for mid-market.
- Burst pricing asked: 1.5x commit rate for usage within burst pool, with maximum burst sustained for 48h windows. Argonaut asked for a guarantee that burst won't exceed 2x baseline without prior notice.
- Overage handling: Argonaut requested a hard cap on overage costs (10% of commit budget per month) and a pre-agreed stepdown policy (auto-throttle if usage >200% for >4 hours). Redwood suggested overage at 1.25x unit rate beyond committed capacity after cap. Needs explicit language in MSA.
- Ramp schedule and credits: Argonaut pushing for ramp credits / monthly true-up so first 3 months bill at 60% of commit rate until steady state is proven. Finance flagged ARR banding requirement for discount thresholds.

Stakeholders & quotes:
- Head of Product (S. Mehta): "We can accept slightly higher latency on edge cases but need predictable tail behavior. Cost predictability is the gating factor."
- VP Eng (D. Torres): "If commit + burst math gives us <30% unit cost vs current hosted spend, we move. Otherwise we stick to hosted + optimize."

Open items / asks for Redwood team:
- Finalize numeric ramp schedule and corresponding billing cadence.
- Define burst SLA: sustained duration, rate multiplier, and preemption policy.
- Hard overage cap language and auto-throttle thresholds in MSA.
- Confirmation of EU data residency (product stores metadata and embeddings for EU customers) and KMS integration details.

Next logistical steps:
- Morgan to circulate redline of proposal to Argonaut procurement by 2026-03-12 (done).
- Legal/finance sync scheduled 2026-03-15 to review MSA redlines.
- Deliverable: finalized proposal with committed GPU counts, burst terms, overage cap, and 3-month ramp credit addendum.
